rubriker.title: KazChess Masters: Lazavik takes title, Smirnov earns GM norm
rubriker._rss_content: Denis Lazavik won the KazChess Masters in Almaty with 6½/9 points, finishing unbeaten after drawing his final-round game against Aram Hakobyan. The 19-year-old Belarusian overtook Daniil Dubov in the penultimate round and eventually finished half a point ahead of the Russian. Another notable result came from 14-year-old Kazakh IM Mark Smirnov, who scored 5½/9, shared third place with Shamsiddin Vokhidov and earned his first GM norm. | Photo: Michal Walusza / FIDE (World Rapid and Blitz Team Championships 2026)

rubriker.title: GothamChess to host new Total Chess highlights show in Budapest
rubriker._rss_content: From November 10 to 20, Budapest will host the first Total Chess tournament, bringing together 24 top players, including Magnus Carlsen. The new format combines Fast Classic, Rapid and Blitz chess to test players across three time controls. The organisers have now announced their broadcast team: Anna Rudolf, Fiona Steil-Antoni, David Howell and Jovanka Houska will cover the tournament, while Levy Rozman, better known as GothamChess, will host a daily highlights show featuring interviews, analysis and special guests.

rubriker.title: Gawain Maroroa Jones wins English Championship 2026
rubriker._rss_content: The open tournament at this year’s English Championships was dominated by the two top seeds. Gawain Maroroa Jones won convincingly, finishing unbeaten with 7½ points out of 9. In round five, he drew with Michael Adams, who also remained undefeated and secured second place, one point behind the winner. In the women's event, Elmira Mirzoeva claimed the title with the same one-point margin over runner-up Anusha Subramanian. | Photos: Official website / Melinda White

rubriker.title: ¿Qué opiniones maneja la prensa deportiva respecto al match entre Gukesh y Sindarov?
rubriker._rss_content: El match por el Campeonato Mundial entre Gukesh y Javokhir Sindarov ha generado una amplia variedad de pronósticos en la prensa internacional, india y uzbeka. Aunque la mayoría sitúa al retador como favorito por su forma reciente, Elo y estabilidad, el campeón conserva argumentos de peso: experiencia mundialista, capacidad de preparación y un techo competitivo elevado. El texto compara esas miradas y examina cómo cada entorno construye su propia narrativa. | Foto: Lennart Ootes / Grand Chess Tour
